title: Import Compliance Manager
description:
JOB SUMMARY:
The Import Compliance Manager is responsible for ensuring the company's import operations comply with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) regulations and all applicable trade laws. This role oversees the accurate classification of imported goods under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS), manages relationships with customs brokers and freight forwarders, and coordinates the end-to-end flow of container shipments from origin to destination, including bonded warehouse operations and duty drawback recovery. The ideal candidate combines deep trade compliance expertise with hands-on experience managing container logistics and import documentation.

JOB DUTIES:

• Manage the classification of imported products under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS), ensuring accuracy and consistency across the product catalog.

• Oversee end-to-end container import operations, including booking, customs clearance, port coordination, and delivery to distribution centers or warehouses.

• Serve as the primary point of contact for customs brokers, freight forwarders, and carriers to resolve clearance delays, documentation discrepancies, and duty disputes.

• Ensure compliance with CBP regulations, Importer Security Filing (ISF) requirements, and other federal import/export regulations.

• Maintain and audit import records, entry summaries, and classification rulings to support recordkeeping requirements and prepare for CBP audits.

• Manage bonded warehouse operations, including inventory control, CBP-mandated recordkeeping, withdrawal entries, and coordination with warehouse operators to ensure compliance with 19 CFR Part 19.

• Monitor changes in tariff schedules, trade agreements, and duty rates (including Section 301, antidumping/countervailing duties) and assess their impact on the business.

• Identify and pursue duty savings opportunities, including free trade agreement eligibility, bonded warehouse deferral strategies, duty drawback, and first sale valuation.

• Administer the company's duty drawback program end-to-end: identify eligible import/export transactions, prepare and file drawback claims, maintain supporting documentation, and manage relationships with drawback service providers or brokers to maximize duty recovery.

• Partner with procurement, finance, and legal teams to evaluate landed cost impacts of tariff changes and sourcing decisions.

• Develop and maintain internal compliance policies, standard operating procedures, and training materials for classification and import processes.

• Manage and mentor import compliance analysts or coordinators, as applicable.

• Track key performance metrics related to container transit times, customs clearance rates, and compliance audit outcomes.

REQUIREMENTS:

• Bachelor's degree in International Business, Supply Chain Management, Logistics, or related field.

• 5+ years of experience in import compliance, customs brokerage, or international trade, with direct experience in HTS classification. Strong working knowledge of CBP regulations, Incoterms, and international shipping documentation (bills of lading, commercial invoices, certificates of origin).

• Experience managing container shipments and coordinating with ocean carriers, freight forwarders, and customs brokers.

• Experience with bonded warehouse (Class 3) operations and duty drawback claim preparation and filing.

• Familiarity with trade compliance software and ERP/TMS systems (e.g., SAP GTS, Oracle GTM, Descartes).

• Licensed Customs Broker (LCB) credential preferred, not required.

• Excellent analytical, organizational, and cross-functional communication skills.

• Ability to manage multiple shipments and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

$90,000 to $120,000, DOE

• Accounts receivable, collections & credit

• Oversee billing accuracy, cash application, unapplied cash research, statements of account, and freight claims.

• Manage the daily relationship with our factoring partner: invoice disputes, liability reporting, remittance details, and new account approvals.

• Administer credit holds and order release in NetSuite; perform credit and risk analysis on new and high-risk accounts.

• Own the AR month-end close and the receivables-related balance sheet accounts: complete reconciliations from HighRadius through to the general ledger and research variances to the transaction level.

• Partner with the General Accounting team at each close to ensure balances reconcile, entries are booked correctly, and reserves are supported.

• Represent receivables in internal, bank, and external audits: prepare schedules and documentation and respond directly to auditor inquiries.

Systems & automation

• Serve as HighRadius administrator and internal product owner: bot mapping, AI training data quality, enhancement requests, and the recurring support and account-management meeting cadence with HighRadius.

• Advance the department’s automation roadmap: expand auto-coding and auto-expensing coverage and identify further processes to automate.

• Act as an AR/credit superuser in NetSuite; partner with IT and Finance on reporting (saved searches, NSAW/Power BI) and on evaluating new automation and AI tools.

title: Head of Finance & Accounting - HCC
description:

This position is responsible for maintaining the financial integrity of the company while providing management with timely, accurate and actionable financial information to support business decisions. The successful candidate will be comfortable working directly with the details of the business while also serving as a key member of the leadership team.

The Head of Finance & Accounting will work closely with Sales, Operations, Manufacturing, Supply Chain and senior management to improve financial visibility, manage costs and working capital, strengthen forecasting, and support profitable growth.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Management Reporting

• Own the company financial reporting and accounting processes, including monthly, quarterly and
annual financial statements.

• Ensure timely and accurate month-end and year-end closing.

• Maintain the integrity of the general ledger, balance sheet and income statement.

• Provide management with clear monthly financial reporting, including actual versus budget and prior-year performance.

• Identify financial risks, unfavorable trends and emerging issues early and bring them to management attention.

• Coordinate with ownership, external accountants, auditors, tax advisors and other financial partners as required. Budgeting, Forecasting & Business Planning.

• Lead the annual budgeting process and maintain a disciplined rolling forecast.

• Develop revenue, gross-margin, expense, EBITDA and cash-flow forecasts.

• Work closely with Sales to evaluate sales forecasts, order intake and expected revenue.

• Provide scenario analysis to support management decisions.

• Translate financial information into practical recommendations for the leadership team.

• Maintain appropriate financial KPIs and management dashboards.
Manufacturing Finance & Cost Accounting.

• Maintain accurate product costing and manufacturing cost information.

• Analyze material, labor, freight, overhead and other manufacturing costs.

• Monitor standard versus actual costs and investigate significant variances.

• Provide visibility into gross margin by product line, customer, channel and other relevant business segments.

• Partner with Operations and Manufacturing to identify opportunities for cost reduction and productivity improvement.

• Support make-versus-buy, outsourcing and supplier decisions through financial analysis.

• Ensure inventory valuation and manufacturing accounting are accurate and properly controlled.

• Cash Flow & Working Capital.

• Maintain short- and medium-term cash-flow forecasts.

• Actively manage accounts receivable, accounts payable and inventory from a working-capital perspective.

• Monitor customer receivables and credit exposure.

• Partner with Operations and Sales to improve inventory turns and reduce slow-moving and obsolete inventory.

• Provide management with early visibility into potential cash-flow or working-capital issues.

Accounting Internal Controls

• Oversee accounts payable, accounts receivable, general accounting and related financial processes.

• Ensure appropriate internal controls and approval processes are maintained.

• Maintain accurate balance-sheet reconciliations.

• Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, tax requirements and company policies.

• Improve financial processes, documentation and controls where necessary.

• Ensure appropriate controls around purchasing, inventory, pricing, credits, expenses and capital expenditures.

Commercial & Sales Support

• Partner with Sales management on pricing, margins, promotions, commissions and customer programs.

• Analyze distributor and dealer performance from a financial perspective.

• Evaluate the financial impact of special pricing, discounts, rebates and promotional programs.

• Support contract and commercial negotiations with appropriate financial analysis.

• Ensure sales incentives and commissions are calculated accurately and consistently with approved programs.

Inventory & Supply Chain

• Provide financial oversight of inventory levels and valuation.

• Monitor inventory turns, excess inventory, obsolete inventory and reserves.

• Work with Operations and Supply Chain on purchasing requirements and inventory planning.

• Provide financial analysis for supplier negotiations, outsourcing initiatives and logistics decisions.

• Support physical inventory counts and ensure appropriate inventory controls.

Leadership & Business Partnership

• Serve as the principal finance partner to the President / General Manager.

• Participate actively in leadership-team meetings and operating reviews.

• Provide objective financial analysis and challenge assumptions when appropriate.

• Establish financial accountability across departments.

• Help department leaders understand their budgets, expenses and financial performance.

• Build a finance function that is responsive, accurate, commercially minded and appropriately scaled for
the business.

Key Performance Expectations
Success in this role will be measured by:

• Accurate and timely monthly financial reporting.

• Reliable forecasts and improved financial visibility.

• Strong control of cash and working capital.

• Accurate inventory and product costing.

• Improved visibility into gross margins and profitability.

• Disciplined expense and overhead management.

• Effective management of receivables and payables.

• Strong financial controls with minimal surprises.

• Clear, actionable financial information for management decision-making.

• Productive partnership with Sales, Operations, Manufacturing and senior leadership.

Qualifications & Experience

• Bachelor degree in Accounting, Finance or related discipline.

• CPA, CMA or MBA is desirable but not mandatory where supported by strong relevant experience.

• Approximately 8-15+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience.

• Prior financial leadership experience within a manufacturing, durable-goods, appliance or similar
product-based business strongly preferred.

• Strong understanding of manufacturing accounting, inventory and cost accounting.

• Demonstrated experience with budgeting, forecasting, cash-flow management and financial analysis.

• Strong knowledge of GAAP and financial controls.

• Experience working with ERP and financial reporting systems.

• Strong Excel and financial modeling capabilities.

• Experience in a small to mid-sized company environment where finance leaders are expected to remain close to the details.

Leadership Profile

•  Hands-on: Willing and able to work directly in the numbers rather than managing solely through
others.

• Commercially minded: Understands that finance exists not only to report results, but to help improve
them.

• Operational: Comfortable working with manufacturing, inventory, supply chain and sales.

• Disciplined: Establishes reliable processes, deadlines and accountability.

• Analytical: Able to identify the business implications behind the numbers.

• Proactive: Identifies problems before they become surprises.

• Pragmatic: Builds processes appropriate for a $25 million entrepreneurial manufacturing business
rather than unnecessary corporate bureaucracy.

• Collaborative: Able to challenge the organization constructively while maintaining strong working
relationships.

• High integrity: Demonstrates sound judgment, confidentiality and professional independence.

$130,000 - $150,000, DOE
